messages:
alice: heads up — we're evaluating integrating an external IBM Cloud HSM for private-edge keystores (on-prem racks + VPC-edge). questions: minimal RBAC for the keystore-proxy SA, what audit events we must capture to prove non-repudiation, network constraints (natless edge), and how to triage a simulated SA compromise. cc @ben @carla @sec-oncall

ben: sounds good. short answer: 1) least-priv SA that CAN ONLY read its own namespaced secret(s) 2) enforce mTLS+ip allowlist to HSM, 3) audit request/response bodies for secret access, 4) have an egress proxy/explicit allowlist for natless edges. :+1:

carla: can you paste the Role/RoleBinding you recommend? also how do we avoid cluster-admin token leaks during CI?

ben: minimal Role (example):
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: keystore-proxy-reader
  namespace: redwood-priv-edge
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get"]
```
and RoleBinding that binds only the keystore-proxy SA in same ns. Do NOT use Secrets mounted as plain files for long-lived tokens; use projected serviceAccount tokens (bound to audience) and short TTLs.

alice: noted. what about audit policy? we need retention requirements for compliance and proof for any KMS decrypts.

maria: capture at least these audit categories: Authentication, Authorization, RequestBody for secrets and execs, and ResponseStatus. Minimal policy snippet: 
```yaml
apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1
kind: Policy
rules:
- level: RequestResponse
  verbs: ["get", "create"]
  resources:
  - group: ""
    resources: ["secrets"]
  - group: ""
    resources: ["pods/exec"]
- level: Metadata
  verbs: ["list", "watch"]
  resources: [{ group: "", resources: ["secrets"] }]
```
Ship audit logs to our SIEM (Splunk/Seq) over TLS, with signed ingestion keys. Ensure logs include pod/sa/namespace and target IP for HSM calls.

sec-oncall: for incident sim — plan below (short):
- create ephemeral SA with the same Role as keystore-proxy but with a distinct name.
- simulate token exfil: cat projected token from pod, then from a different namespace try to call our keystore-proxy endpoint.
- in parallel, run a KMS decrypt attempt against the HSM IP using that token.
- verify SIEM alerts: failed auths, unusual src-ns, and an alert on "keystore-decrypt" spike.
- revoke SA, rotate keystore-proxy secret, and validate canary decrypts succeed/fail accordingly.
This exercise should take ~30–45m and surfaces both RBAC gaps and audit gaps.

carla: network policy question — edge nodes are NATless, HSM requires fixed source IPs. recommendation?

ben: two patterns:
1) egress-proxy (recommended): all pods talk to internal egress proxy. Proxy has fixed egress IP(s) and mTLS to HSM. Netpols restrict pod -> proxy port only.
2) hostRoute/allowlist: restrict node egress to HSM IPs, but this couples nodes to secrets. less flexible.
Example NetworkPolicy allowing only keystore-proxy to HSM via egress-proxy svc: 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: keystore-proxy-egress
  namespace: redwood-priv-edge
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-proxy
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: egress-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8443
```

alice: great. anything about KMS client configs? key wrapping vs direct decrypt?

maria: prefer envelope encryption: local keystore-proxy holds customer keys encrypted with HSM-wrapped KEK. Proxy sends only wrapping/unwrapping operations to HSM; limit decrypt surface. Also enable HSM audit/logging (if supported) and fetch HSM logs into SIEM.

sec-oncall: vuln triage note — if a CVE shows in the keystore-proxy image (e.g., CVE-2025-XXXX in an openssl lib), do:
1) create pod disruption schedule -> cordon nodes running proxy pods
2) build patched image, run canary in staging-edge (same network profile)
3) in prod apply canary -> if decrypt latencies are fine, rollout to rest
4) if exploit detected, rotate KEKs and revoke affected SA tokens.

carla: what alerts should we create immediately?

ben: minimal alert set:
- unexpected namespace access to /v1/keystore (anomaly by SA)
- spike in keystore decrypt ops from single SA/pod
- failed auths to HSM from approved IPs
- missing audit logs for a time window > 1m
- keystore-proxy image mismatch from approved digest

alice: ok assigning tasks:
- @carla: create Role/RoleBinding PR + CI check to forbid cluster-admin in keystore pipeline (ETA EOD)
- @ben: netpol + egress-proxy helm chart review (ETA 2d)
- @maria: audit policy + SIEM ingestion config (ETA 1d)
- @sec-oncall: run the compromise sim next Tue and capture playbook notes (ETA Tue)

deploy-bot: reminder: rolling-update will start 2026-03-26T02:00Z if PR merged (automated schedule).

alice: thanks all — I'll drop the HSM IPs and a small test vector in the PR. anything else? :eyes:
